summary: Host-plant gardens alive with free-flying butterflies near the Statue of Unity, best in the first sunny hours of the morning.
description:
The Butterfly Garden plants its way to its residents: beds of host and nectar species (citrus, milkweeds, lantana relatives, curry-leaf) that keep local butterfly populations breeding on site rather than behind netting. On a warm, sunny mid-morning the paths flicker with them; on an overcast afternoon you will mostly see plants, which is the honest trade of a living exhibit.

Interpretation boards cover life cycles and species; kids get caterpillar-hunting on the host plants with a little guidance. It is a light, pleasant forty minutes that lands best with children and macro photographers, folded into the jetty-zone loop with the Cactus Garden next door.
highlights: Free-flying butterflies on living host plants
Life-cycle spotting for kids, eggs to chrysalis
Quick pairing with the Cactus Garden

modes.road: On the campus circuit; e-buses stop nearby

fees.note: Per person, sold online. Verified Aug 2026

visit.notes: Butterfly activity tracks sun and warmth. 09:00–11:30 is the window.

seasonality.notes: Post-monsoon months carry the biggest populations.

experience.photography_notes: Macro or a long lens at mid-morning; move slowly and shoot nectaring stops rather than chasing flight.

warnings: No catching or handling, enforced for the colony's sake

emergency.nearest_hospital: Ekta Nagar facilities; Rajpipla civil hospital (~25 km)

tips: Schedule it mid-morning between bigger attractions
Overcast day? Deprioritise it: activity drops with the sun
